clauses.notes: DESIGNED DEVIATION. Reference: decoding_order = argsort((mask*chain_mask + 1e-4) * |randn|), a fresh random permutation per number_of_batches draw with fixed (and missing) positions sorted first. The fixed-first property is probabilistic, not hard: a designed/fixed pair flips when |randn_designed| < ~1e-4*|randn_fixed| (per-pair probability of order 1e-4; recon_math is right, recon_protocol's 'always' overstates). aminx native default: deterministic N->C (arange) order; fixed tokens are pre-seeded into the carry but are only VISIBLE to a designed position if they precede it in N->C order, so a designed residue does not condition on fixed residues C-terminal to it. Consequences: (i) sampled sequences are a different conditional factorisation from the reference's, so token/marginal statistics differ even with identical weights; (ii) no order randomness across samples. Reference-compatible mode EXISTS: pass a host-built WaveScheduleBundle (build_inference_bundle(wave=...), WaveScheduleBundle.from_tie_groups) carrying the reference argsort order -- this is what the spec's exact tier does. aminx has no built-in generator of the reference fixed-first formula (see random_order_fixed_first).

clauses.notes: Reference masked pairs get distance D_max (the row's largest valid distance), so they TIE with the farthest valid partner; aminx uses a strictly larger sentinel (inf / 1e4 / 1e8), so masked partners always rank after every valid one. Identical neighbour sets whenever a row has >= k valid partners. For rows with < k valid partners (short or gapped chains; masked residues' own rows), the reference's choice among {farthest valid, masked...} falls to torch tie-breaking and can DROP the farthest valid neighbour in favour of a masked one, while aminx always keeps all valid partners then takes masked ones by lowest index. Masked neighbours still feed the decoder's structure branch (mask_fw uses the row mask only), so this can change logits on gapped inputs. Also the ligand path's first RBF uses the sentinel distance for masked pairs (1e4 vs D_max).
